subsystems.name: Lattice problem core
subsystems.role: defines the hard mathematical problem whose difficulty underpins all security.

subsystems.name: Key generation
subsystems.role: creates a public key and a private key from random lattice points and small errors.

subsystems.name: Encryption and encapsulation
subsystems.role: encodes a shared secret or message using the public key, adding noise to hide it.

subsystems.name: Decryption and decapsulation
subsystems.role: recovers the secret with the private key and corrects for the added noise.

subsystems.name: Digital signatures
subsystems.role: proves authenticity and integrity using lattice-based signature schemes.

subsystems.name: Implementation layer
subsystems.role: makes the algorithms fast and safe on real processors and hardware.

buildSteps.title: Choose a hardness assumption
buildSteps.detail: Select a lattice problem, such as Learning With Errors, that is believed hard even for quantum computers.

buildSteps.title: Design the scheme
buildSteps.detail: Construct key generation, encryption and decryption using polynomial arithmetic modulo a prime, with carefully chosen noise.

buildSteps.title: Prove security
buildSteps.detail: Reduce the scheme's security to the underlying lattice problem and analyse parameters against known classical and quantum attacks.

buildSteps.title: Standardise
buildSteps.detail: Submit the design to a public standardisation process, invite years of open cryptanalysis, and select stable algorithms.

buildSteps.title: Implement efficiently
buildSteps.detail: Write constant-time software and use number-theoretic transforms for fast polynomial multiplication.

buildSteps.title: Test and validate
buildSteps.detail: Run official test vectors, check side-channel resistance, and formally verify critical code paths.

buildSteps.title: Integrate into protocols
buildSteps.detail: Embed the algorithms in TLS, VPNs, messaging apps and hardware security modules, often in hybrid mode with classical cryptography.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and migrate
buildSteps.detail: Roll out to production, then gradually phase out RSA and elliptic-curve cryptography as confidence grows.

prerequisites.why: the entire security proof rests on these problems remaining hard for quantum computers.

prerequisites.tech: Quantum computers capable of running Shor's algorithm at scale
prerequisites.why: the threat model that motivates lattice encryption, though full-scale machines do not yet exist.

prerequisites.tech: Fast modular arithmetic and number-theoretic transforms
prerequisites.why: makes lattice cryptography practical on ordinary processors.
prevents attackers from stealing keys through timing, power or electromagnetic leaks.
builds trust and ensures different systems can interoperate.

pathway.milestone: NIST published the first post-quantum standards in 2024, including lattice-based ML-KEM and ML-DSA
pathway.unlocks: a stable, internationally recognised basis for quantum-resistant encryption.

pathway.milestone: Hybrid deployment in browsers, VPNs and messaging apps, mixing lattice encryption with classical methods
pathway.unlocks: protection against 'store now, decrypt later' attacks without abandoning current security.

pathway.milestone: Hardware acceleration and secure elements for lattice algorithms
pathway.unlocks: quantum-resistant cryptography on phones, smart cards and industrial devices.

pathway.milestone: Full migration of critical infrastructure away from RSA and elliptic curves
pathway.unlocks: a global financial and communications system that remains secure even if large quantum computers arrive.
